question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP, GitHub edge region iad

headers.www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_request", error_description="No access token was provided in this request", resource_metadata="https://api.githubcopilot.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/"

decoded.body: bad request: missing required Authorization header
decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 200; authorization_servers: https://github.com/login/oauth; 10 scopes: repo, read:org, read:user, user:email, read:packages, write:packages, read:project, project, gist, notifications
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://github.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/login/oauth; PKCE S256; grants authorization_code, refresh_token, device_code; NO registration_endpoint; scopes_supported: offline_access only

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to the hosted GitHub MCP server answers 401 and names its protected-resource metadata in the challenge; a bare GET answers the same. The metadata is readable without a credential and lists ten GitHub scopes, while the authorization server it names advertises exactly one scope, offline_access, PKCE S256, and the authorization_code, refresh_token and device_code grants. It advertises NO registration_endpoint, so a client cannot register itself: a human must create a GitHub App or OAuth app first. That is the fact an agent operator needs and it is not in the vendor's prose. No authenticated request was made, so what the server does with a credential is not measured here. One IP, one sample, one moment.

reproducibility.command: curl -sS -i -X POST https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"public-agents-researcher","version":"1.0"}}}'
